transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Connor (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of Search - AtlanticSearch), Ethan (ML Eng), Sara (CTO), Tom (Infra)

Summary (auto): brief discovery on embeddings + rerank architecture, vector DB options, throughput and security needs.

[00:00] Connor: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have people on the call from AtlanticSearch, can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Priya: Yeah this is Priya, Head of Search, quick hello.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan here, ML eng, I run their search infra team.
[00:20] Sara: Sara, CTO, I'll jump in on architecture and compliance.
[00:25] Tom: Tom, infra lead.
[00:28] Connor: Awesome, I m Connor from Redwood, AE, and with me are Maya and Jules from our solutions eng team. Quick agenda: current stack and pain points, embeddings + rerank goals, throughput and SLAs, security and deployment preferences, and next steps.
[00:46] Maya: Cool, and last thing we'll do is outline what a pilot might look like.
[00:52] Priya: Great. So to kick off, high level we're a vertical search product for travel reviews. We currently run BM25 + TF-IDF retrieval plus a light neural reranker. We want to move to embeddings-based retrieval with a neural rerank step to improve semantic recall.
[01:12] Ethan: Our current QPS averages 500 during peak, but during big promos it spikes to ~1.2k. Latency target for user-facing search is 150-200ms p95, our backend budget for rerank+retrieve is ~120ms.
[01:32] Connor: Ok, good, that helps. Are you generating embeddings in-house or using a hosted model?
[01:37] Ethan: We currently compute embeddings offline with an internal model (768 dim) but we re looking at moving to 1536-dim open models for better quality and to align with signal in our content.
[01:48] Maya: Typical tradeoff there is quality vs index size and ANN performance. With 1536 dims you need more memory per vector and ANN tuning. Are you currently using Faiss or a managed store?
[02:00] Tom: We have a self-hosted cluster running Faiss on CPU nodes; not ideal. We've been experimenting with Redis vector search and Pinecone in a dev env.
[02:10] Jules: Understood. From Redwood's side, we support both Hosted and Dedicated deployments. For throughput like 1k+ QPS and strict latency SLOs you guys mentioned, many customers opt for Dedicated capacity so you get reserved GPU pools and predictable latency.
[02:26] Sara: Curious about the vector DB part — would Redwood replace that or sit in front of it? How do you recommend integrating?
[02:33] Maya: Redwood is an inference platform. For embeddings retrieval you can either: 1) call Redwood's embeddings API and index into your vector DB (e.g., Redis/Pinecone/Weaviate), or 2) use Redwood end-to-end where we host embeddings + ANN indexing in a hosted workflow. Most big customers keep their vector DB for search because they need custom indexing (metadata, hybrid fields) and we integrate with it.
[02:57] Priya: When you say integrate—what does that look like in terms of latency? If we compute embeddings via Redwood Hosted and then query our Redis cluster, what's the extra hop?
[03:07] Maya: Typically embedding generation is tiny, tens of ms per call for batch sizes >16 depending on model. The primary latency is ANN query time on your vector DB. If you push ANN into Dedicated GPUs with Redwood managing ANN, we can give better end-to-end p95 by co-locating the rerank model and embeddings execution. But many customers index into Redis and run ANN there.
[03:28] Ethan: We re leaning toward keeping Redis because of our metadata and hybrid search (BM25 + vector). How does Redwood support hybrid search?
[03:36] Jules: We recommend a hybrid pipeline: use BM25 to get candidate set (e.g., top 200-1000), then compute embeddings and run ANN over the candidates or full vector index—then do a lightweight cross-encoder rerank on the top K. For rerank we can host the cross-encoder on Redwood and return scores to apply in your ranking.
[03:55] Priya: For our traffic patterns this sounds fine, but the rerank budget is small. How many items can the cross-encoder score per query within that 120ms budget?
[04:03] Maya: It depends on model size. A distilled cross-encoder on a GPU can score 64-128 pairs in ~40-80ms. For larger cross-encoders you need batching and more GPUs. There s also options to use asymmetric rerankers: use a bi-encoder for dense retrieval and a small transformer for rerank to reduce latency.
[04:26] Ethan: Any data on memory per vector for 1536 dims? We re worried about storage costs in Redis.
[04:32] Jules: Rough estimate: float32 1536 dims = ~6KB per vector; with quantization (e.g., int8 or product quantization) you can drop to 512-1k per vector. That affects ANN accuracy so it's a trade. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[04:50] Tom: For Dedicated, what's the networking model? We need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS.
[04:56] Maya: Dedicated supports VPC/VPN peering or Private Link, and for Private deployments we offer a customer-controlled control plane and KMS/HSM integration. We also provide audit logs for compliance.
[05:08] Sara: SOC2 and ISO compliance are musts. Do you have the artifacts?
[05:12] Connor: Absolutely — we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs. We'll also send a short architecture note showing how KMS and audit log flows work with Dedicated or Private.
[05:22] Priya: Back on retrieval — we have a legacy inverted index we can't drop yet, so hybrid is critical. Would Redwood's SDK help glue BM25 + ANN?
[05:31] Jules: Yes, our SDKs include helpers for hybrid workflows and rerank pipelines and examples for Redis + Redwood reranker calls.
[05:39] Ethan: On throughput: 1k peak QPS, each query needs embedding generation for user query and then 200 candidate rerank. So we re looking at end-to-end budgets, possible batching on queries, and caching.
[05:52] Maya: You can cache frequent queries or use prefix KV cache. Redwood also supports batching across requests to improve GPU utilization for embeddings and rerank models. The tricky part is latency-sensitive queries where you can't batch. For those we keep a low-latency pool.
[06:06] Tom: For 1k qps with 200 candidates and a small reranker, what kind of Dedicated footprint are we talking about?
[06:12] Maya: Very rough: if you run an optimized bi-encoder + small cross-encoder, maybe 4-8 GPUs for production to meet 200ms p95 with headroom. We'll need to run a pilot benchmark to get precise numbers.
[06:23] Priya: Pilot would be great. We'd want to run our query logs and see end-to-end latency comparison between current Faiss and Redwood Dedicated with Redis integration.
[06:33] Connor: Perfect next step — we'll send a pilot plan + sizing worksheet.
[06:38] [long pause, side conversation muted]
[06:52] Ethan: Another question: embedding dimensionality — do you recommend 1536 or 512? Bigger is better for semantic, but cost and index complexity rise.
[07:02] Jules: For travel review domain 1536 often helps capture nuance, but 512 with a stronger training pipeline can be competitive. Also consider using asymmetric encoders: higher-dim document vectors, smaller query vectors.
[07:16] Priya: How about retraining frequency? We have frequent content updates.
[07:20] Maya: You can do incremental indexing; many customers push deltas and reindex nightly for the rest. If you use Redwood embeddings hosted, you can compute embeddings at ingestion and store them in Redis. For offline batch re-compute we recommend using a job that hits Redwood's batch embedding endpoints.
[07:38] Tom: Security again — do you keep customer data? What's retention?
[07:42] Connor: For Hosted we retain logs per your config; for Dedicated we can configure zero retention of payloads depending on contract. Private gives you full control. We'll include retention options in the slide.
[07:54] Sara: Cost model question — pricing per token for generation is standard but embeddings + dedicated sizing?
[07:59] Connor: Hosted embeddings are per-embedding unit; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits. We'll give a ballpark in the worksheet.
[08:09] Priya: Who from our side should be in the technical deep-dive? Tom and Ethan likely. Possibly our infra SRE.
[08:16] Connor: Sounds good. We'll propose times next week.
[08:20] Priya: Any limitations on number of dimensions supported in the ANN you host?
[08:24] Jules: No hard limit — runtime supports typical dims up to 4096. The constraints are memory and ANN index type.
[08:32] Ethan: For the rerank model, do you host both bi-encoder and cross-encoder?
[08:36] Maya: Yes. We can host bi-encoders for retrieval and cross-encoders for rerank. You can mix and match per route. Also support for model variants and automatic fallback to smaller models under load.
[08:50] Tom: Is there a way to run A/B tests—like 10% traffic to Redwood rerank vs our current in-house?
[08:55] Jules: Absolutely, Redwood Console supports route-level rollouts, canary percentages, and automatic fallback policies.
[09:03] Priya: We'll need regression monitoring — if quality dips after a model change we need alerts.
[09:08] Maya: Redwood Optimize ties eval sets to rollouts and will alert on quality regressions.
[09:14] Ethan: For benchmarks, what metrics do you usually collect? Latency p50/p95, cost per query, recall@k, rerank NDCG?
[09:22] Jules: Yes, all of those plus token-level cost breakdowns and GPU utilization. We'll produce a spreadsheet with suggested experiments.
[09:32] [11:00 minute marker - conversation proceeds in more granular transcript; timestamps jump when speakers change quickly]
[11:04] Priya: One more practical: do you provide connectors for Redis upserts or is that on our side?
[11:10] Maya: We provide SDKs and some ingestion helpers but indexing/upserts to your Redis cluster would be performed by your infra. For Private deployments we can help with migration scripts.
[11:22] Ethan: How do we handle metadata filtering with ANN? We rely heavily on faceted filters (date, region, content type).
[11:28] Jules: Use hybrid: filter by metadata first (candidate generation) then run ANN only on filtered subset. Many vector DBs support metadata-aware ANN queries; otherwise do a two-phase query.
[11:40] Priya: Any risks of semantic drift if we change embedding models too often?
[11:44] Maya: Yes — that's why we recommend binding eval sets and running offline A/Bs before rollouts. Also Redwood has model version pinning for routes.
[11:55] Tom: What's the pilot timeline realistically? 4-6 weeks?
[11:59] Connor: Typical pilot 3-6 weeks: ingest sample corpus, run benchmarks, iterate models, and show production-like metrics.
[12:07] Priya: Ok that works.
[12:10] [brief recap by Connor]
[12:12] Connor: Recap: you need embeddings + rerank to replace current pipeline, keep Redis for metadata/hybrid search, target p95 150-200ms, peak ~1.2k qps, prefer Dedicated but open to Hosted pilot. Next steps: we (Redwood) send sizing/pricing, SOC2/ISO docs, benchmark plan, and propose times for deep-dive.
[12:34] Priya: Yep, thanks.
[12:37] Sara: Thanks all.
[12:40] Connor: I'll send notes and action items.
[12:44] [call ends]

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings, product names sometimes transcribed differently (e.g., penccone instead of Pinecone).
questions: Can Redwood integrate seamlessly with Redis for hybrid search?
What Dedicated footprint is required for 1k-1.2k QPS with a 200-candidate rerank?
How does Redwood support quantization for 1536-dim vectors?
What are the retention and KMS options for Dedicated/Private?
